metadata.title: PIRLS 2011 User Guide for the International Database
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a user guide for the PIRLS 2011 International Database rather than an empirical analysis paper. It describes how to access and analyze PIRLS 2011 and prePIRLS 2011 data using IEA IDB Analyzer and SAS/SPSS, including the availability of sampling stratification variables and derived variables. Because no specific analytic subsample or weighting variable (e.g., student/sampling weights or replicate weights) is applied in the text excerpt, the guide does not report whether complex survey weights are used in any particular model. For secondary analyses, users are expected to follow the PIRLS/TIMSS Methods and Procedures documentation for the study’s complex sampling design and to apply the appropriate weights/replicate weights when producing population-representative estimates and standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a data documentation/user guide that describes the structure and contents of the PIRLS 2011 International Database, not an empirical study estimating predictive models or reporting PV-based outcomes. Plausible values and missing-data handling strategies are therefore not operationalized as part of a reported analysis in the provided text. Missing-data handling is not specified because the guide excerpt focuses on database components (files, codebooks, item parameters) and analysis tools rather than a concrete analytic pipeline with an outcome and model results.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The user guide states that the PIRLS 2011 International Database makes available achievement and background data for 48 countries and 9 benchmarking participants, with data from 334,446 students. No analytic subsample restrictions (e.g., grade-only, module-only, or complete-case filtering) are described in the provided excerpt because this is not an empirical analysis; it is a description of the released database contents.

data.outcome_summary: PIRLS 2011 is an international large-scale assessment of reading achievement administered after four years of primary schooling (fourth grade), conducted on a regular five-year cycle with assessments in 2001, 2006, and 2011. The PIRLS 2011 International Database also includes prePIRLS 2011 for countries whose students are earlier in learning to read; prePIRLS uses shorter and easier texts and places less emphasis on higher-order reading skills. The database release provides not only student achievement data but also background questionnaire data for students, parents, teachers, school principals, and curricular information, along with item information and IRT item parameters. The guide emphasizes that secondary analyses should be conducted using IEA IDB Analyzer and SAS/SPSS tools and should be aligned with the complex sampling procedures and variable construction described in the accompanying Methods and Procedures documentation. Benchmarks and trends can be examined across cycles for participating countries, while new participants can use 2011 results for comparative standing.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a PIRLS 2011 user guide for the International Database, not an empirical research article. As such, it does not specify an analytic research design, does not train or evaluate machine learning models, and does not report target-variable performance metrics or effects. Consequently, fields related to PV handling in an analysis context, missing-data handling in a specific model, and ML techniques/findings are not applicable to the provided excerpt.
